title: Fleet Overview
description: Health, resources and best load-test results for every server.

list.name: Deploys
list.expr: max by (commit) (o11y_build_info) unless max by (commit) (o11y_build_info offset 2m)

links.title: Run a load test
links.tooltip: Start a load test against one server (one at a time)

options.content: ### Self-hosted observability for 13 HTTP servers Every server below implements the same API ([OpenAPI spec](https://github.com/rshdhere/load-test/blob/main/servers/openapi.json)) in a different language and framework, runs in its own container, and is health-checked every 5 seconds. Load tests are driven by k6 and streamed into Prometheus. Source: [github.com/rshdhere/load-test](https://github.com/rshdhere/load-test). **▶ Run a load test** against any server and watch it live, or **⚔ race 2-3 servers** head to head. One test runs at a time. See who wins on the **[Leaderboard](/d/leaderboard)**, or put servers next to each other in **[Compare servers](/d/compare-servers)**.

panels.title: Servers up
panels.description: Servers whose /api/v1/health check passed on the last probe, out of 13.

panels.title: Availability
panels.description: Share of passing health checks across the fleet over the time range, while monitoring was running.

panels.title: Median health latency
panels.description: Median time for a health check to complete, across all servers.

panels.title: Server CPU
panels.description: CPU used by all 13 server containers, as a share of one core (200% = 2 cores).

panels.title: Server memory
panels.description: Working-set memory of all 13 server containers.

panels.title: Load-test requests
panels.description: HTTP requests sent by k6 load tests within the time range.

panels.title: Load test now
panels.description: Whether a visitor-started load test is running, and against which server.

panels.title: Visitor tests
panels.description: Load tests started by visitors within the time range.

panels.title: Reliability · 99.9% of health checks pass, over a rolling 30 days
Servers within objective
panels.description: Servers whose health checks passed at least 99.9% of the time over the last 30 days, out of 13.

panels.title: Least budget left
panels.description: The server closest to missing its objective, and the share of its error budget it has left. Load tests that make a server miss health checks spend its budget.

panels.title: Error budget left by server
panels.description: Share of each server's 30d error budget (0.1% of health checks) still unspent. Below zero means the objective is missed.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: Alerts firing or about to fire right now. Empty is good.

panels.title: All servers
panels.description: Live status and resource use for every server, plus its best load-test result in the time range. Click a server to open its dashboard.

panels.title: Availability timeline
panels.description: Health-check result per server over time. Red bands are outages.

panels.title: CPU by server
panels.description: CPU each server container is using right now, as a share of one core.

panels.title: Memory by server
panels.description: Working-set memory per server container.

panels.title: Best peak req/s
panels.description: Highest request rate each server sustained in a load test within the time range.

panels.title: Memory by language
panels.description: Working-set memory of each language's servers combined, right now.

targets.expr: sum by (language) (server:container_memory:working_set * on (server) group_left (language) max by (server, language) (probe_success{job="server-health"}))

panels.title: CPU by language
panels.description: CPU used by each language's servers combined, over the last minute.

targets.expr: sum by (language) (server:container_cpu:rate1m * on (server) group_left (language) max by (server, language) (probe_success{job="server-health"}))

panels.title: Memory per server, by language
panels.description: Average idle footprint: a language's memory divided by its number of servers.

targets.expr: sort_desc(sum by (language) (server:container_memory:working_set * on (server) group_left (language) max by (server, language) (probe_success{job="server-health"})) / count by (language) (probe_success{job="server-health"}))
